svg.text: The piece funnels from a broad problem (how do neurons process information?) down through a formal tool (PID) and
then fans out into converging empirical findings, before closing with limits and a summary that loops back to the

g.text: A funnel: broad question narrows to the PID method, which then opens into several empirical findings that converge on
one message, followed by limits and future work.

g.title: How do brains process information? — New recording tech and analysis methods now make this tractable. — → spya-yb735k
Mutual information & transfer entropy track flow — Measure dependence and directed information flow between neurons. — → spya-ygkzd8
But flow alone can't show how inputs combine — → spya-dhy39x
g.text: But flow alone can't show how inputs

g.title: Partial Information Decomposition (PID) — redundant, unique, synergistic atoms — Splits joint information into interpretable pieces via a lattice. — → spya-u0wm5e
Synergy concentrates in rich clubs — → spya-e3ghxj
Recurrent connections boost synergy — → spya-p8by2y
Synergy peaks at moderate correlation — → spya-zfs2z7
In monkeys, task shifts synergy vs redundancy — → spya-aqcngt
Caveats: cultures, bivariate estimates — → spya-vjzxxm
Practical limits: data type, sample size, lattice explosion — → spya-kmgwhs
Future: local & multi-target PID — → spya-zz5xxs
Neurons compute on patterns, not just totals — → spya-rc5z33

g.text: A chain: from the puzzle that whole ≠ sum of parts, through the two-source special case, to the general lattice, ending
at the unresolved choice of redundancy measure.

g.title: Whole vs sum of parts: synergy or redundancy? — → spya-u0wm5e
Two-parent case: redundant+unique+synergistic atoms — → spya-y7wdb7
Equations underdetermined without more info — → spya-y7wdb7
General case: partial information lattice — Mobius inversion over a partially ordered set of sources yields each atom. — → spya-k378fv
Which redundancy measure to use? — → spya-d2quz5
No single accepted answer; choice depends on data — → spya-d2quz5

g.text: Several independent lines of empirical evidence, from cortical cultures and behaving monkeys, converge on the same
idea: synergistic computation is concentrated and context-dependent.

g.title: Hundreds of cultured neurons, thousands of triads analyzed — → spya-cc282b
Synergy tracks feedforward transfer entropy — → spya-cc282b
Rich club: 40% of neurons, ~88% of synergy — → spya-e3ghxj
Recurrent connections raise synergy; feedback does not — → spya-p8by2y
Synergy peaks at ~7% of max correlation, then falls — → spya-zfs2z7
Caveats: bivariate TE, in vitro only — → spya-vjzxxm
Macaques: redundancy rises during motor execution — Synergy dominates generally, but shifts with task phase and region. — → spya-aqcngt

g.text: Two parallel extensions of PID, both relaxing the classic framework's restriction to one moment and one target.

g.title: Classic PID: one target, expected values only — → spya-zz5xxs
Local PID: time-resolved, per-moment decomposition — Reveals distinct computational profiles during neuronal avalanches. — → spya-z39m3x
Multi-target / temporal PID (ΦID) — Linked to consciousness loss and brain genetic architecture in fMRI studies. — → spya-xn6y4f
Both are new; many open questions remain — → spya-xn6y4f
g.text: Both are new; many open questions
